divorce.d: The legal dissolution of a marriage.
divorce.e: Richard obtained a divorce from his wife some years ago, but hasn't returned to the dating scene.

dock.d: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially common dock, and used as potherbs and in folk medicine, especially in curing nettle rash.

domestic.d: A house servant; a maid; a household worker.
domestic.e: 2005: Bellingham-Whatcom County Commission Against Domestic Violence, Domestic Violence in Whatcom County (read on the Whatcom County website athttps//web.archive.org/web/20060618212243/http://www.co.whatcom.wa.us/boards/dv_whatcom042505.pdf on 20 May 2006) - The number of “verbal domestics” (where law enforcement determines that no assault has occurred and where no arrest is made), decreased significantly.

dominate.e: The dominant party controlled the government.

donate.d: To make a donation; to give away something of value to support or contribute towards a cause or for the benefit of another.
donate.e: He donated an etching from his own collection to the new art gallery.

donation.d: A voluntary gift or contribution for a specific cause.
donation.e: They were collecting donations for the elderly at Christmas.

dorm.e: I haven't seen Emily since I dormed with her in our student days.

draft.d: A current of air, usually coming into a room or vehicle.
draft.e: I'd rather have a fresh, cheap draft beer.

drain.d: A conduit allowing liquid to flow out of an otherwise contained volume; a plughole (UK)
drain.e: The drain in the kitchen sink is clogged.

dread.e: My visit to the doctor is filling me with dread.

dreadful.d: A shocker: a report of a crime written in a provokingly lurid style.

drought.d: A period of unusually low rainfall, longer and more severe than a dry spell.

dynamic.d: A characteristic or manner of an interaction; a behavior.
dynamic.e: Watch the dynamic between the husband and wife when they disagree.

eagle.d: Any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.

ease.d: Lack of difficulty; the ability to do something easily.
ease.e: He played the ukelele with ease.

effectively.d: In an efficient or effective manner; with powerful effect.

elite.d: A special group or social class of people which have a superior intellectual, social or economic status as, the elite of society.

emphatically.d: In an emphatic manner; with emphasis.
emphatically.e: The leaders feel emphatically that each side must prove good faith before they'll will resume their talks.

employ.d: The state of being an employee; employment.
employ.e: The school district has six thousand teachers in its employ.

employee.d: An individual who provides labor to a company or another person.
employee.e: One way to encourage your employees to work harder is by giving them incentives.

employer.d: A person, firm or other entity which pays for or hires the services of another person.

endlessly.d: In an endless manner; continuously without limit.

endorse.d: A diminutive of the pale, usually appearing in pairs on either side of a pale.

enduring.d: Long-lasting without significant alteration; continuing through time in the same relative state.

energy.d: The impetus behind all motion and all activity.

enforce.d: To keep up, impose or bring into effect something, not necessarily by force.
enforce.e: The police are there to enforce the law.

engagement.d: An appointment, especially to speak or perform.
engagement.e: Check the gears for full engagement before turning the handle.

engulf.e: Depression engulfed her after her daughter's death.

enquire.e: He enquired about the availability of rental bicycles in the town.

enrol.d: UK, New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, and Canada standard spelling of enroll.

enroll.d: To enter (a name, etc.) in a register, roll or list
enroll.e: They were eager to enroll new recruits.

enterprise.d: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
enterprise.e: Biosphere 2 was a scientific enterprise aimed at the exploration of the complex web of interactions within life systems.

entrepreneur.d: A person who organizes and operates a business venture and assumes much of the associated risk.

environment.d: The surroundings of, and influences on, a particular item of interest.

erect.d: Upright; vertical or reaching broadly upwards.
erect.e: The penis should be fully erect before commencing copulation.

eruption.d: A violent ejection, such as the spurting out of lava from a volcano.
eruption.e: There was an eruption of joy at the final whistle.

estate.d: The collective property and liabilities of someone, especially a deceased person.

evacuate.d: To leave or withdraw from; to quit; to retire from
evacuate.e: The firefighters told us to evacuate the area as the flames approached.

evaluate.d: To draw conclusions from examining; to assess.
evaluate.e: It will take several years to evaluate the material gathered in the survey.

evolve.d: To move in regular procession through a system.

excel.d: To surpass someone or something; to be better or do better than someone or something.
excel.e: I excelled everyone else with my exam results.

exceptionally.d: To an unusual, remarkable or exceptional degree.

excessive.d: Exceeding the usual bounds of something; extravagant; immoderate.
excessive.e: Putting a wide vibrato on a single 16th triplet note at 160 beats per minute seems rather excessive.

exclude.d: To bar (someone) from entering; to keep out.
exclude.e: to exclude young animals from the womb or from eggs

exclusively.d: (focus) to the exclusion of anything or anyone else; solely or entirely

exquisite.e: Sourav Ganguly scored an exquisite century in his debut Test match.

extensive.d: Having a great extent; covering a large area; vast
extensive.e: I have done extensive research on the subject.

eyebrow.d: The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.

fabulous.d: Of or relating to fable, myth or legend.

facilities.d: Facilities for urination and defecation: a toilet; a lavatory.
facilities.e: The facility she shows in playing the violin is unrivalled.

factor.d: A doer, maker; a person who does things for another person or organization.
factor.e: The factor of the trading post bought the furs.

faculty.d: The academic staff at schools, colleges, universities or not-for-profit research institutes, as opposed to the students or support staff.
faculty.e: She transferred from the Faculty of Science to the Faculty of Medicine.

faith.d: A trust or confidence in the intentions or abilities of a person, object, or ideal from prior empirical evidence.
faith.e: I have faith in the goodness of my fellow man.

fame.d: What is said or reported; gossip, rumour.

familiarise.d: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of familiarize.

familiarize.d: To make or become familiar with something or someone.
familiarize.e: I took some time to familiarize myself with the layout of her kitchen before I got to cooking for her.

fantastically.e: He painted fantastically with everything as if in a dream.

fascinated.d: simple past and past participle of fascinate

fascination.d: The act of bewitching, or enchanting
fascination.e: To my fascination, the skies turned all kinds of colours.

fatal.d: A fatality; an event that leads to death.

fate.d: The presumed cause, force, principle, or divine will that predetermines events.
fate.e: The oracle's prediction fated Oedipus to kill his father; not all his striving could change what would occur.

faulty.d: Having or displaying faults; not perfect; not adequate or acceptable.
faulty.e: I don't think you can infer that from the premise. It's a faulty argument.

fed up.d: simple past and past participle of feed up
fed up.e: After two days, I am fed up with this nonsense.

federal.d: A law-enforcement official of the FBI; a federal agent.

feedback.d: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
feedback.e: After you hand in your essays, I will give both grades and feedback.

fibre.d: A single piece of a given material, elongated and roughly round in cross-section, often twisted with other fibres to form thread.
fibre.e: The cloth was made from strange, somewhat rough fibre.

fierce.d: Exceedingly violent, severe, ferocious, cruel or savage.
fierce.e: A fierce storm battered the coast.

flesh.d: The soft tissue of the body, especially muscle and fat.

flutter.d: To flap or wave quickly but irregularly.
flutter.e: The eagle soared across the horizon with just a few slow flutters of its wings. The flutter of insects and bats is more rapid. Some birds also use non-flight flutters as communication and in thermoregulation.

foresee.d: To be able to see beforehand: to anticipate; predict.

foul.d: Covered with, or containing unclean matter; dirty.
foul.e: A ship's bottom is foul when overgrown with barnacles

found.d: To encounter or discover by accident; to happen upon.
found.e: I found my car keys. They were under the couch.

fraud.d: The crime of stealing or otherwise illegally obtaining money by use of deception tactics.

frugal.d: Avoiding unnecessary expenditure either of money or of anything else which is to be used or consumed; avoiding waste.

fundamental.d: (usually in the plural) A leading or primary principle, rule, law, or article, which serves as the groundwork of a system; an essential part
fundamental.e: A need for belonging seems fundamental to humans.

funk.d: Foul or unpleasant smell, especially body odor.

generalisation.d: The formulation of general concepts from specific instances by abstracting common properties.

generalise.d: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of generalize.

generalization.d: An act or instance of generalizing; concluding that something true of a subclass is true of the entire class.

generalize.d: To speak in generalities, or in vague terms.

generously.d: In a generous manner, in a way that is giving or ample.
generously.e: He generously donated what little he could.
